description:
Stahleck Castle (Burg Stahleck) stands on a crag above the medieval town of Bacharach, at the mouth of the Steeg valley on the Rhine, about 50 km south of Koblenz. It was built for the Archbishops of Cologne. The name comes from Middle High German stahel (steel) and ecke (crag), and the first recorded holder, Goswin von Stahleck, is mentioned in 1135. In the 12th century it was the seat of the Counts Palatine of the Rhine. The castle is part of the UNESCO Upper Middle Rhine Valley, listed in 2002.

According to tradition, Agnes, daughter of Count Palatine Conrad of Hohenstaufen, secretly married Henry of Brunswick, son of Henry the Lion, here in early 1194, in what became known as the Stahleck (or Bacharach) Marriage. During the Thirty Years' War the castle was besieged and taken eight times. Elector Palatine Karl Ludwig had it repaired in 1666, and a stone tablet in the courtyard records the work. On 15 March 1689, during the War of the Palatine Succession, French troops blew it up and left it in ruins.

In 1909 the ruin passed to the Rhenish Association for Landmark Preservation. From 1925 the architect Ernst Stahl rebuilt it as a youth hostel, following Matthäus Merian's 1646 engraving; the hostel was dedicated in June 1926, with further rebuilding in the 1930s and in 1965–67. In 1942 schoolboys and students from Luxembourg were interned at the castle as punishment for protesting against forced conscription, and a memorial plaque recalls them. A water-filled section of the rock-cut moat survives in front of the shield wall.

Today the castle is a youth hostel with about 168 beds, run by the Rhineland-Palatinate youth hostel association. Guests of any age can stay, in private doubles or dormitories from about €25 per person per night. The castle is not open for tours, but the courtyard is open to the public and has views over the Rhine.

how_to_visit:
**Getting there:** Bacharach is on the west bank of the Rhine, about 50 km south of Koblenz. Frequent Rhine Valley trains on the Koblenz–Mainz line stop at Bacharach station; the castle is a 20-minute walk uphill from the station through the medieval town walls. Rhine cruise ships also stop at Bacharach in summer.

**Tickets:** Entry to the courtyard is free; there are no interior tours. The castle is a youth hostel (Burg Stahleck). Overnight stays can be booked via Booking.com or through the DJH youth hostel website.

**Practical tips:** The courtyard is open to visitors during the day, with no ticket desk or timed entry required. The youth hostel accepts guests of all ages — advance booking is strongly recommended in summer and during wine-harvest weekends.

**Combine with:** [Marksburg Castle](/castles/germany/marksburg-castle), the only Rhine valley castle never destroyed, lies about 25 km north near Braubach and makes a natural same-day pairing. [Stolzenfels Castle](/castles/germany/stolzenfels-castle) near Koblenz is another well-preserved Rhine gorge fortress within easy reach.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to stay at Stahleck Castle?
faqs.answer: Beds start from about €25 per person per night, a youth hostel rate per person rather than per room. The castle has dormitories and private rooms. Check current prices and availability on Booking.com.

faqs.question: Can you visit Stahleck Castle without staying?
faqs.answer: Yes, the courtyard is free to enter and has views over the Rhine. The castle is a youth hostel and is not open for interior tours.

faqs.question: Who can stay at the youth hostel?
faqs.answer: Anyone. Burg Stahleck youth hostel is open to all ages (youth hostels in Germany are not restricted to young people). Advance booking is strongly recommended.

faqs.question: How do you get to Stahleck Castle?
faqs.answer: Take a train on the Koblenz–Mainz line to Bacharach station, then walk about 20 minutes uphill through the medieval town. Rhine boats also stop at Bacharach in summer.

faqs.question: What is the history of Stahleck Castle?
faqs.answer: Stahleck was built for the Archbishops of Cologne above Bacharach, and its first recorded holder, Goswin von Stahleck, is mentioned in 1135. It was taken eight times in the Thirty Years' War and blown up by French troops in 1689. From 1925 the architect Ernst Stahl rebuilt it as a youth hostel, dedicated in June 1926.

faqs.question: Is the castle part of a UNESCO site?
faqs.answer: Yes — Burg Stahleck is within the Upper Middle Rhine Valley, a UNESCO World Heritage Site recognised for its combination of castles, medieval towns, and vineyards along 65 km of the Rhine gorge.

faqs.question: What is the town of Bacharach like?
faqs.answer: Bacharach is a medieval town on the Rhine with 14th-century town walls, half-timbered houses and a Romanesque church, a convenient base for exploring the gorge.

hotel.non_guest_access_note: The courtyard is open to day visitors whether or not you book a bed, and has views over the Rhine; the castle is not open for tours. See How to Visit above
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** Bacharach, Rhineland-Palatinate — same access as described in How to Visit above.

**Rooms & rates:** Private double rooms and multi-bed dormitories are inside the rebuilt castle itself. From about €25 per person per night (hostel rate, per person), including bedding; breakfast, half-board and full-board options available.

**On-site:** Hostel restaurant/dining hall; the courtyard described in How to Visit is open to both overnight guests and day visitors.

**Good to know:** Open to guests of all ages, not just young people. The hostel has about 168 beds. Overnight stays can be booked via Booking.com or through the DJH youth hostel website.

**Combine with:** Marksburg Castle and Stolzenfels Castle, both within easy reach — see the recommendations above.
